messages:
Mike L: Heads-up — Marigold LoRA merge went into the nightly quant pipeline (q4b_v2). Quick smoke eval shows a large embedding stability drop for invoice identifiers.

Anya R: ugh. Can you paste the eval short summary? :eyes:

Mike L: eval-bot posted summary below (ran on marigold-invoices-50):
```
rwd-eval v2.1
run_id: marigold-lora-q4b-smoke-2026-03-21
dataset: marigold-invoices-50 (50 examples)
metric: embedding_cosine_stability (baseline=fp16)
baseline (fp16): median_cosine = 0.92
q4b_v2 (4-bit): median_cosine = 0.58
delta = -0.34
weirdness: invoice-number queries dropped to 0.35-0.55
```

Sonal: That magnitude is not normal for a LoRA merge. Could be quant packing mismatch or a token remap. Was tokenizer changed?

Kevin: I ran a quick cosine histogram locally — many examples containing numeric tokens moved below 0.6. Looks like some ids/amount tokens collapsed to different embedding neighborhoods after q4b.

Eva: Any chance it's a KV-cache or compilation path problem? Did the compile flags change for long/short context kernels?

Mike L: No seq-len flags changed. Runtime is rwd-runtime 3.7.2, quant-compiler q4b_v2. Config used for smoke: 
```
model: marigold-lora-v1
merge: lora-customer-marigold-2026-03-20
quant: q4b_v2
batch_policy: dynamic
cache_policy: enabled
```

Anya R: Quick repro command I used: `./tools/rwd-embed-check --model marigold-lora-v1 --quant q4b_v2 --n 100 --metric cosine` -> median 0.61.

eval-bot: Added run to dashboard: https://console.redwood/evals/1234 (notes: "embedding flip detected; customer impact potential: high")

Sonal: Can we shadow test int8 and q4b_v1 to isolate? If int8 matches fp16 then q4b_v2 is suspect.

Kevin: Ran int8 shadow: median_cosine = 0.89 (delta -0.03). Ran q4b_v1: median_cosine = 0.85 (delta -0.07). So q4b_v2 is the outlier.

Eva: Good. Next steps: 1) stop rollout for q4b_v2 on Marigold (hold). 2) run operator-level diff (quant packing tables) between v1 and v2. 3) collect a small sample of token-level embedding vectors for numeric tokens pre/post.

Mike L: I'm holding the rollout now and emailing SE contact. Running operator diff now. Patch commands: `rwd-quant-diff --base q4b_v1 --head q4b_v2 --model marigold-lora-v1 --dump ops`

Anya R: If this is kernel packing bug, rollback to q4b_v1 + run full quickpack to confirm. ETA for a confirmation run?

Kevin: I can trigger a 200-sample quickpack on q4b_v1 in ~15m and post the report.

Mike L: Kevin's report posted: q4b_v1 quickpack median_cosine=0.86, top-5 invoice queries stable. Recommend rollback for Marigold, and open a quant-compiler issue. :thumbsup:

Sonal: Agree. Also request upstream test that checks numeric-token neighborhoods specifically — add to our regression set.

Eva: I'm filing the compiler issue and adding a small targeted test in the quant CI. Also logging customer comms draft for SE: "We've paused the new quant path for your model and are reverting to the previous quantization; we expect no change to semantics while we investigate."

Mike L: Sending the rollback now. Roll command: `rwd-deploy rollback --model marigold-lora-v1 --quant q4b_v1 --env nightly --reason "q4b_v2 embedding instability"`

eval-bot: Rollback completed in nightly cluster. Follow-up run queued: https://console.redwood/evals/1235

Anya R: Nice. After we triage, let's add a short doc in eng-ml/quant-notes about what to watch for on customer LoRAs — numeric token checks + embed histograms.

Kevin: I'll extract the 10 worst-offending examples and put them in the bug report.

Mike L: Thanks team. Good fast triage. I'll update the Marigold SE and close the loop once compiler team responds. :white_check_mark:
